title: Decide what a cross-tenant membership is allowed to mean
goal: The contract states that one user may belong to multiple tenants (section 2.2, invariant 1), and the product ships both a login tenant picker and a TenantSwitcher for exactly that case. But authorization is tenant-owned: replaceUserRoles stamps system_user_role.tenant_id from the user's owning tenant (user_helper.go:83-108), RoleService.ensureUsersExist is tenant-scoped (role_helper.go:301-307), and GetUserRolesForTenant filters by the claimed tenant (login_runtime.go:328-338). A membership in a second tenant therefore grants login and switching but no roles, no menu and 403 on every protected API, with no UI or API able to assign a role there. This packet does not implement anything: it records the maintainer's choice between narrowing the membership semantics (A), making role binding cross-tenant (B) and removing multi-tenant membership (C), with the cost and the failure case of each. W4 depends on the signed decision.
findings: TC-01 (P1): a user can hold an active membership in tenant B while every role binding it owns lives in tenant A, so the login picker offers B and the resulting session has an empty role set. TenantSwitcher.tsx:22-34 already documents the same reasoning for platform-capable subjects but not for ordinary multi-membership users.
The existing e2e constructs this exact scenario (tenant-hostile-browser-matrix.spec.ts:82-92) but asserts only that the app shell renders after choosing B (:138-140), so the defect is not caught.

A decision is required before code because the three resolutions change different contracts: A keeps section 2.2's invariant but narrows what a membership implies; B changes the ownership model of role bindings; C removes a shipped user-facing capability.

Where the three read points actually live (verified 2026-10-27): pkg/tenant/authz.go:159-180 DiscoverDefaultTenant, pkg/tenant/authz.go:313-343 ListActiveMembershipsForUser (the candidate list), modules/auth/login/login_tenant_switch.go:39-83 ListSwitchableTenants. DiscoverDefaultTenant already denies with ErrTenantForbidden when more than one active membership exists, so today the picker is the only path a multi-membership subject can take.

Option A does not break the platform viewpoint: TenantSwitcher hides itself for platform-capable subjects (TenantSwitcher.tsx:31-72) and those are served by TenantViewpointSwitcher through X-Tenant-Id, which reads tenants, not memberships. Filtering the membership paths only affects ordinary subjects.

Filtering must not touch ListActiveMemberships (pkg/tenant/membership.go): /auth/current uses it to attach the caller's own membership role (login_tenant_switch.go:100-120), which must keep reporting what the membership row says even when that membership is not loginable.

in: Produce docs/reviews/TENANT_MULTI_MEMBERSHIP_DECISION_2026-10-27.md with one row per option: what changes, what data or contract text changes, the failure case it fixes, the new failure case it can introduce, and the cost

Option A: narrow AddMember to users owned by the tenant (system_user.tenant_id = tenantID) and filter the three login read points (DiscoverDefaultTenant, ListActiveMembershipsForUser, ListSwitchableTenants) to tenants where the subject has at least one IAM role binding; because a subject can never own roles in two tenants, this makes the login picker and TenantSwitcher unreachable, so option A also removes those two UI controls while keeping the endpoints as filtered compatibility surfaces; contract clarifies that a cross-tenant membership grants no permissions and is not offered

Option B: allow cross-tenant role binding. AddMember accepts role_ids and writes system_user_role with the target tenant; ensureUsersExist accepts users that are live members of the target tenant; contract redefines 'user owning tenant' versus 'binding tenant'. Record that replaceUserRoles currently deletes all of a user's bindings across tenants and would have to be scoped to the target tenant first
Option C: remove multi-tenant membership. Drop the login picker and TenantSwitcher, make membership single-tenant, amend contract section 2.2, and record the data migration as a separate packet
Record the recommendation (A for V1, B as a V2 workstream) and the exact follow-up packet ids
State explicitly that the decision does not authorise automatic cleanup of existing cross-tenant membership rows
out: Implementing any option in this packet
Deleting or cleaning historical membership rows
Changing the contract text before the decision is signed
Choosing B or C without naming the implementation packet and its risks

implementationNotes: This is a decision packet: a wave that changes no source file is a valid closeout.

For option B, the decisive detail is that replaceUserRoles deletes `WHERE user_id = ?` (user_helper.go:88) with no tenant predicate. Under B, editing a user in one tenant would wipe its bindings in every other tenant. Any B decision must carry that fix as a prerequisite.

For option A, the filtering belongs at three read points, not one: DiscoverDefaultTenant, ListLoginTenantCandidates and the switchable endpoint. Filtering only the picker leaves auto-resolution able to stamp an unusable claim. The underlying functions are in pkg/tenant/authz.go, so one predicate there can serve all three.

Do not filter ListActiveMemberships itself. /auth/current reports the caller's membership role from it, and a membership that is not loginable must still be reported as what it is, not hidden as absent.
Do not propose an implicit membership-role to IAM-role mapping in any option; contract section 2.2 forbids it.
Every option must name what happens to the existing rows produced by the current AddMember. 'Leave them and hide them from login' is acceptable only if written down.
